claims.text: Over 60% of the United States population is classified as overweight or obese based on body mass index thresholds.
Approximately 85% of adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus are also classified as obese.
Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus independently increase cardiovascular disease morbidity and mortality by greater than 2-fold.
Subcutaneous white adipose tissue constitutes approximately 80% of all adipose tissue in lean, healthy individuals.
Omental white adipose tissue produces 2-fold to 3-fold higher levels of interleukin-6 than subcutaneous white adipose tissue.
Macrophages represent approximately 5% to 10% of total cells within lean adipose tissue.
Macrophages represent up to 60% of all cells present within obese adipose tissue.
Human resistin protein shares 59% sequence homology with mouse resistin protein.
Approximately 60% of ectopic hepatic triglycerides in obese non-alcoholic fatty liver disease patients originate from adipose tissue free fatty acid release.
Approximately two-thirds of the obese human population exhibits excessive pancreatic fat deposition.
Bariatric surgery yields an estimated 48% reduction in macrovascular events in patients with obesity after more than 5 years.

evidence.description: "Obesity has now reached epidemic proportions, with over 60% of the US population classified as overweight or obese (defined by a body mass index ≥ 25 or 30 kg/m 2, respectively)"
"Recent epidemiological evidence has shown that 85% of type 2 diabetic adults are also obese"
"both obesity and T2DM increase the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), increasing morbidity and mortality by greater than 2-fold"
"subcutaneous WAT is the most prominent WAT depot in lean, healthy subjects, making up ∼ 80% of all adipose tissue"
"Omental fat produces 2 to 3-fold higher levels of IL-6 than subcutaneous fat"
"Reported to represent ∼ 5–10% of total cells within lean adipose tissue, macrophages in obese adipose tissue represent up to 60% of all cells present"
"macrophages in obese adipose tissue represent up to 60% of all cells present"
"Human resistin is only 59% homologous to mouse resistin ( 106), which has raised some controversy over the pathogenic role of resistin"
"It has been estimated that nearly 60% of ectopic hepatic triglycerides in obese NAFLD patients derive from FFA released from adipose tissue"
"reports that nearly 2/3 of the obese population has excessive pancreatic fat"
"A recent meta-analysis has estimated that on average, patients exhibit a 48% reduction in macrovascular events with a 79% reduction in mortality more than 5 years following bariatric surgery"

methodologies.name: Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DEXA) and Computed Tomography (CT)
methodologies.description: Imaging modalities used to assess body fat distribution, lean mass composition, and regional ectopic adipose tissue accumulation.

methodologies.name: 18F-FDG PET/CT Imaging
methodologies.description: Positron emission tomography using 2-[18F]fluoro-2-deoxyglucose to identify and quantify functional, metabolically active brown adipose tissue in humans.

limitations.text: Standard clinical measures like BMI, waist circumference, or body weight fail to accurately depict anatomical fat distribution or distinguish metabolically healthy from metabolically unhealthy obesity phenotypes.
Human resistin shares only 59% sequence homology with mouse resistin, limiting direct translational comparisons between animal models and human metabolic disease.

Surgical weight loss studies primarily sample subcutaneous adipose tissue due to sampling feasibility, leaving the precise impact of bariatric surgery on visceral adipose tissue inflammation insufficiently evaluated in humans.

Methods of inducing white adipose tissue browning via cold exposure or beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonists are clinically impractical due to rapid reversibility, high time demands, and adverse cardiometabolic effects.

future_work.text: Elucidate mechanisms of white adipose tissue browning that are long-lasting and operate independently from the sympathetic nervous system.
Investigate whether individuals possessing inherently low brown adipose tissue activity are predisposed to metabolic syndrome or if metabolic pathology actively suppresses BAT function.
Determine the exact physiological role of adipocyte-derived FGF21 and whether it predominantly acts locally or contributes to circulating hormone pools across varied nutritional states.
